opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: The labs: developing new vaccines and drugs. Down 31% — big Phase 3 respiratory trials wound down, plus deliberate cost cuts across the company.

opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Sales teams, offices, admin. Down 12% — consulting and outside services cut back.

follow100Note: R&D alone eats $114 of every $100 of revenue — Moderna spent $1.54 billion running the business against $678 million of sales. The $826 million loss was covered from its $8.1 billion cash pile, not from this quarter's sales.
footerNote: Loss quarter: the $826M shortfall is covered by cash on hand.
oneTimers: $144M of inventory write-downs sits inside Q4 cost of sales ($291M for the full year) — unsold vaccine stock written off as demand shrinks. It is not a separate line item, but it is a big reason cost of sales stays high even as sales fall.

Cash of $8.1B at December 31 includes a $600M initial draw on Moderna's $1.5B credit facility — borrowed money, not operating cash. Without it, the year-end balance would have been $7.5B, down from $9.5B a year earlier.
otherDetail: Interest income of $70M, less $12M of other expense — net $58M.

segments.name: Net product sales
segments.note: Selling vaccines — mainly COVID shots, $264M in the U.S. and $381M abroad. Down 31% as COVID vaccine demand keeps shrinking.

segments.name: Other revenue
segments.note: Grants, collaborations, licensing and royalties — plus new stand-ready manufacturing revenue from long-term partnerships.

takeaways.text: Revenue of $678M vs $966M a year ago, almost all of it lower COVID vaccine volume. Yet the net loss narrowed to $826M from $1.12B: costs fell faster than sales, with R&D down 31% and cost of sales down 39%.
takeaways.title: Revenue fell by nearly a third — but the loss shrank

takeaways.text: Management targets up to 10% revenue growth in 2026 — roughly half U.S., half international — with R&D of about $3.0B, cost of sales of about $0.9B, and year-end cash of $5.5–6.0B. The cost-cutting that saved 2025 is now the plan, not a one-off.
takeaways.title: 2026: growth returns, costs keep falling

takeaways.text: Spikevax, mNEXSPIKE and mRESVIA are now three approved products. The flu vaccine filing was accepted in the EU, Canada and Australia but got a Refusal-to-File letter from the U.S. FDA; the norovirus Phase 3 trial is fully enrolled with a readout expected in 2026.
takeaways.title: Three approved products, and the pipeline is doing the talking

verdict: Moderna lost $826 million in Q4 as COVID vaccine sales fell 30%, but the loss narrowed from $1.1 billion a year ago because deep cost cuts — R&D down 31% — outpaced the revenue decline, and management now promises growth again in 2026.
